issues.legal_issue: An unaided private educational society is not a State under Article 12 merely because it runs schools and performs the public function of imparting education.
A private body performing a public duty is amenable to judicial review under Article 226 only when the challenged action has a public-law element.

A service dispute between employees and an unaided private educational institution, governed by an ordinary contract and not statutory service provisions, is not maintainable in a writ petition under Article 226.
The doctrine of legitimate expectation applies in the realm of public law and does not govern contractual relations between private parties.
